name: Huawei UB Link 2.0 (Ascend 950DT scale-up / unified addressing)
version: UB Link 2.0, Ascend 950DT generation (Atlas 650E 8-NPU, Atlas 950 SuperPoD 64-NPU, 1024-NPU pod)
bandwidth_basis: PER NPU, PER DIRECTION, INTRA-SERVER (8-NPU Atlas 650E) - the larger figure in notes is the 16-NPU full-mesh case. DIRECTION IS STATED BY HUAWEI, which is what makes this record usable and is the reason it is filed at confidence 0.8 rather than contested. The Atlas 650E page (cn-huawei-atlas-650e-spec) gives UB Link as '8 x 784 GB/s BIDIRECTIONAL intra-server' and '2 x 8 x 1.68 TB/s' for the 16-NPU full-mesh, so the recorded value is 784 / 2 = 392 GB/s per direction per NPU for the 8-NPU configuration. READ THE 'x' CAREFULLY: Huawei's notation '8 x 784 GB/s' is 8 NPUs each at 784, not 784 shared eight ways. The SuperPoD page (cn-huawei-atlas-950-superpod-spec) independently gives '64 x 1.68 TB/s BIDIRECTIONAL UB Link' for the 64x 950DT cabinet, i.e. 1.68 TB/s per NPU bidirectional = 840 GB/s per direction per NPU - the 16-NPU full-mesh figure, and the 840 = 2 x 392 x ... no: 1.68 TB/s / 8 NPU per group x 2 groups = the doubled rate that the 2 x 8 notation encodes. THE SCALE-OUT FIGURE IS SEPARATE AND PER-DIRECTION ALREADY: UBoE and RoCE at '400 Gbps per NPU UNIDIRECTIONAL', which is 50 GB/s per direction and must NOT be halved - the same vendor uses bidirectional for UB Link and unidirectional for RoCE in the same sentence group, so mixing them is easy.
topology: Two scale-up domains at different rates, which is unusual and is the interesting property of this record. INTRA-SERVER: 8 NPUs on the Atlas 650E (14U air-cooled, ~14.5 kW, 2 x 950 CPUs), 8 x 96 GB on-chip memory = 768 GB, 4.0 TB/s peak memory bandwidth per server. FULL-MESH: 16 NPUs at the doubled 1.68 TB/s bidirectional per NPU, i.e. Huawei publishes a wider non-mesh-free domain than the 8-way that AMD's Infinity Fabric and NVIDIA's NVSwitch both top out at. SUPER-POD: the 44OU Atlas 950 SuperPoD cabinet holds 64 NPUs at ~100 kW liquid-cooled and scales to 1024 NPUs, '1.72 PB/s UB Link' across the pod, which is 1.72 PB/s / 1024 = 1.72 TB/s per NPU bidirectional, or 860 GB/s per direction - essentially flat with the 16-NPU full-mesh rate, meaning Huawei scales bandwidth with NPU count rather than holding a flat per-chip figure.
switching: No switch part is named in the retrieved sources; the 16-NPU full-mesh and 64-NPU/1024-NPU domains are described as fabric configurations without a switch SKU. Scale-out is a different mechanism entirely: UBoE (Huawei's Ultra Backbone Ethernet) and RoCE at 400 Gbps per NPU unidirectional.
notes: Added 2026-10-03 to resolve a DANGLING REFERENCE: huawei-ascend-950dt listed 'huawei-ub-link' in its interconnect array and no such record existed, so a validator pass reading that array had nothing to resolve. The figures were already on the accelerator record; this is the interconnect view of them, with the direction conventions made explicit. FIRST-PARTY PUBLISHED (Atlas 650E / Atlas 950 pages): 8 x 96 GB on-chip memory, 4.0 TB/s peak memory bandwidth, 12.48 PFLOPS mxFP4 / 6.43 PFLOPS mxFP8-FP8-HiF8 / 3.40 PFLOPS FP16-BF16 per 8-NPU server; UB Link 8 x 784 GB/s bidirectional intra-server and 2 x 8 x 1.68 TB/s for 16-NPU full-mesh; UBoE and RoCE 400 Gbps per NPU unidirectional; PCIe 5 x16; SuperPoD 64x 950DT at 64 x 1.68 TB/s, scaling to 1024 NPUs at 1.72 PB/s with '256 TB unified global memory addressing'. THE UNIFIED-ADDRESSING CLAIM IS THE HEADLINE AND IT IS AN INFERENCE RESULT, not a fabric result: a KV cache addressable as one flat space across 1024 NPUs, rather than replicated per rank, changes the memory model in a way no NVLink generation does, and it is why this part is worth a record even though its bandwidth is not exceptional. THE BANDWIDTH IS ACTUALLY EXCEPTIONAL IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS: 392 GB/s per direction per NPU against 500 GB/s of local memory bandwidth is a ratio of 0.78, versus H100's 450/3350 = 0.13 and even MI355X's 537.6/8000 = 0.067. That is the inverse of the Ascend 910B problem recorded on huawei-hccs, where ~90 GB/s of chip-to-chip bandwidth against ~1.2-1.6 TB/s of contested memory bandwidth made wide TP expensive. On the 950DT the fabric is within the same order as local memory, so TP is essentially free on bandwidth grounds - and the B* crossover in docs/11-interconnect-decision.md lands in the tens of thousands, far beyond any serving batch. THAT IS THE HEADLINE FINDING OF THIS SLICE'S AUDIT: the part with the worst-known scale-up fabric (910B, HCCS, no primary source) has been superseded by a generation whose scale-up fabric is the best ratio in this repo, and the improvement is entirely in the ratio rather than in absolute per-link bandwidth. CONTRAST WITH THE PREDECESSOR, explicitly, since it is not apples to apples: the 910C used SMIC 7 nm and HBM2e, the 950DT uses on-chip memory, and Huawei publishes no process node for the 950DT - so the fabric improvement cannot be cleanly separated from the memory-substrate change. CAVEAT: all figures are VENDOR THEORETICAL and Huawei's own page carries the disclaimer 'Theoretical computing power may have a <1% error in actual testing' - these are clock-derived peaks, not measurements, and no third-party measurement of UB Link bandwidth is held in this repo. KIND: filed as 'other' because UB Link has no entry in the schema's interconnect enum and is not a member of any named family; note the easy confusion with 'UBoE', Huawei's Ultra Backbone ETHERNET scale-out interface, which is a different thing at a different rate and direction - see the bandwidth_basis above.
